title: Chapter 59 — Builder Programs & Volume Agreements
intro: Structuring formal builder programs with tiered pricing, volume commitments, and delivery priority.

sections.title: Program Structure
sections.content:
A builder program formalizes the relationship. Instead of ad-hoc quoting on every project, the builder gets pre-negotiated pricing tiers based on annual volume commitment.

Tier 1 (5-10 projects/year): standard trade pricing, same-day quoting, dedicated rep. Tier 2 (10-25 projects/year): 5-8 percent additional discount, priority delivery windows, quarterly business reviews. Tier 3 (25+ projects/year): best pricing, dedicated delivery days, annual rebate on volume, and co-marketing support.

The program creates switching costs. Once a builder is enrolled in your Tier 2 program with priority delivery and discounted pricing, moving to a competitor means starting over at Tier 1 pricing somewhere else.

sections.title: Volume Tracking
sections.content:
Track actual versus committed volume quarterly. If a Tier 2 builder committed to 15 projects and is tracking at 8, have the conversation early: 'You are at 8 through Q2. If we do not hit 15 by year-end, the tier resets. What can we do to capture more of your projects?'

This is not a threat — it is a partnership conversation. Maybe they had fewer projects. Maybe they split volume with a competitor on a category you could cover. Either way, the data tells you what is happening.

sections.title: Program Marketing
sections.content:
Promote your builder program actively. Feature it on your trade webpage. Mention it in every first meeting with a new builder prospect. Create a one-page program summary — tiers, benefits, contact info — that you can leave at job sites and trade events.

The builder who knows you have a formal program perceives you as a professional trade partner, not a retail store that sometimes serves builders. That perception difference wins accounts.
